_concept: ALGORITHMS — a first-class asset class, not content hidden inside scripts
_one_line: The value of an analysis product IS its algorithms. Everything else — the data, the findings, the documents — is either an input to them or an output of them.

_why_first_class.the_audit: The asset registry declared five kinds — gold_table, store, tool, doc, gold_database — all of them ARTIFACTS. Zero algorithms. The techniques existed only as implicit content inside scripts, which made them invisible: we could not say which algorithm runs where, reuse one deliberately, compare ours against the market's, or improve one and know what it affected.
_why_first_class.the_market_argument: What a buyer pays Celonis or Signavio for is not their storage and not their dashboards — it is conformance checking, variant analysis, object-centric mining. The algorithms ARE the product. Ours being undeclared meant the product was undeclared.
_why_first_class.the_sharper_argument: An algorithm fails differently from a tool. A broken tool fails loudly. A subtly wrong algorithm produces confident, plausible, WRONG output. This session produced four: a greedy classifier rule that stole FTBB from bank statements; a substring matcher that linked 337 claims to 'CO'; a wrong denominator that made a 35% gap of which half was a category error; a swallowed generic error that masked an invalid field for three runs. You cannot review what you have not named.
_why_first_class.the_portability_argument: A tool is one binding of an algorithm to one problem, one schema, one tenant. The ALGORITHM is what travels to installation #2. Data ages, findings age, tools are bindings — algorithms compound.

_fields.operates_on: the data class it consumes — logs / process events / repository / data / model / interfaces
_fields.origin: MARKET_STANDARD (adopted) · MARKET_EXTENDED (adopted and improved) · OURS (no market equivalent)
_fields.bound_in: the tool(s) that implement it — an algorithm with no binding is a paper
_fields.failure_mode: how this algorithm produces a WRONG answer without failing loudly

A1_chunked_temporal_read.does: read a purging log in bounded time windows (<=6h) because a wide call hangs and the connection degrades every ~12 calls
A1_chunked_temporal_read.failure_mode: a silently truncated window looks like a quiet period in the data
A1_chunked_temporal_read.improve: derive the chunk size from observed response time instead of a constant

A2_rolling_window_accumulation.does: capture a window the source purges (7-120 days) into *_history tables, turning a window into a history
A2_rolling_window_accumulation.market_equivalent: NONE — commercial tools connect live and inherit the system's retention
A2_rolling_window_accumulation.why_fragile: gitignored, unversioned, writing to a local database with no confirmed backup — and it cannot be back-filled at any price
A2_rolling_window_accumulation.failure_mode: a missed day is invisible: the history simply has a hole nobody sees
A2_rolling_window_accumulation.improve: make 'days of history captured' a first-class metric; version the script

A3_two_axis_classification.does: explain every call on two independent axes — PROCESS (from the object name) and ORIGIN (from host/destination/user)
A3_two_axis_classification.why_extended: process mining assigns activities but does not systematically resolve WHO CALLED. Without origin, a middleware call and an internal report are indistinguishable.
A3_two_axis_classification.produced: the 80.6%-external finding; 91.1% of business calls explained
A3_two_axis_classification.failure_mode: an unresolved origin collapses a fleet into one label — 174 middleware endpoints currently read as one caller
A3_two_axis_classification.improve: resolve endpoint GUIDs from the middleware side; SAP cannot name them
A3_two_axis_classification.gated: GATED s097: 10 golden cases over classify_origin/classify. The ORIGIN axis is what the cases protect — MULESOFT, BRIDGE-RFC and SMTMSBP must never read as people, and OUR OWN extraction must be excluded or we measure ourselves as the business.

A4_ordered_classifier_ladder.does: ordered rule chain (package -> software component -> overlay -> name -> text -> substrate); first match wins, specificity expressed by ORDER
A4_ordered_classifier_ladder.failure_mode: ORDER-DEPENDENCE IS SILENT. A greedy early rule steals from a later one and nothing errors. Proven twice in s097: 'FTB' swallowed FTBB (bank statements) into deal management; an inline comment swallowed two dict entries and moved 70,766 executions between domains.
A4_ordered_classifier_ladder.improve: replace the package-regex rung with the DF14L component lookup, which is authoritative. Regex becomes the fallback, not the primary. THIS IS PRIORITY 2 OF THE WHOLE MODEL.

A5_adaptive_learning_loop.does: auto-resolve unknown calls by function group / naming / app domain, LEARN the resolution, re-classify until convergence, expose the remainder as an explicit frontier
A5_adaptive_learning_loop.why_it_matters: the closest thing the model has to learning — each run explains more with zero hand-coding
A5_adaptive_learning_loop.failure_mode: a rule learned WRONG persists forever and invisibly — DEMONSTRATED on its first run with the new signal: mapping the broad technical bucket Basis_Security to one business process taught it that IDOCS_OUTPUT_TO_R3, IDOC_INBOUND_ASYNCHRONOUS and BAPI_EXCHANGERATE_GETDETAIL are identity management. 7 rules purged; the mapping removed so it cannot be relearned. Returning NOTHING is correct for a technical call: it goes to the frontier for human review, which is where it belongs. Precision beats coverage when the engine remembers its mistakes.
A5_adaptive_learning_loop.improve: give it the reads/writes signal (C3) so it can resolve custom FMs that have no curated overlay entry
A5_adaptive_learning_loop.fed_by: C1/C1b/C1c component resolution — the authoritative rung, s097
A5_adaptive_learning_loop.result_s097: 8 -> 25 learned rules, +17 ALL from the authoritative signal, zero hand-coding. Coverage 92.7%. Frontier 224 FMs / 225,568 calls (7.3%), mostly kernel FMs not in TFDIR at all.

A6_frontier_with_substrate_tier.does: coverage % + explicit worklist, with a third tier for technical substrate (connectivity, session, monitoring): real execution, legitimately non-business
A6_frontier_with_substrate_tier.produced: unexplained execution fell from 40% to 11.7% without hiding anything
A6_frontier_with_substrate_tier.failure_mode: substrate becomes a dumping ground if it is ever matched before business rules — it is matched LAST on purpose
A6_frontier_with_substrate_tier.improve: watch the TREND, not the size: a frontier that stops moving means the discovery loop stopped running

B1_dfg_discovery.does: build the process map from an event log — activities as nodes, observed transitions as edges
B1_dfg_discovery.market_equivalent: pm4py — the reference implementation (van der Aalst lineage), the substrate Celonis and Signavio productised
B1_dfg_discovery.failure_mode: a DFG on the wrong case notion produces a plausible map of a process that does not exist
B1_dfg_discovery.improve: two event sources are wired (transactions AND change documents); the change-document source is richer for lifecycle and under-used

B2_variant_analysis.does: group cases by exact path, rank by frequency and cost — the long tail is where exceptions live
B2_variant_analysis.failure_mode: variants computed on a truncated log look like process simplicity

B3_performance_bottleneck.does: cycle time per transition; waiting versus processing
B3_performance_bottleneck.failure_mode: timestamps from different systems make a bottleneck out of a clock skew

B4_declarative_conformance.does: state the normative rules, classify every case against them, quantify the deviation in money
B4_declarative_conformance.why_it_matters: THIS IS WHERE THE PRODUCT LIVES — the delta between AS-DESIGNED and AS-RUN
B4_declarative_conformance.proven: P2P: 3-way match, GR strictly before IR — 38% conformant, 70 IR-before-GR violations, $713,341 exposure
B4_declarative_conformance.failure_mode: applying a market normative model without checking the tenant's real shape. A standard O2C model here would report 100% non-conformance because there are ZERO deliveries — a false finding.
B4_declarative_conformance.improve: exists for exactly ONE flow. The four public-sector flows have no normative model at all. THIS IS PRIORITY 3.

B5_ocel2_object_centric.does: one event references MULTIPLE object types, with no forced single-case notion
B5_ocel2_object_centric.why_it_matters: ahead of most commercial tooling. Flat single-case mining forces an artificial case ID and distorts anything convergent or divergent — which public-sector finance is constantly: one budget, many commitments, many actuals.
B5_ocel2_object_centric.failure_mode: choosing object types badly reproduces the single-case distortion in a more expensive format
B5_ocel2_object_centric.improve: this is the correct substrate for budget-to-actual, where 'the case' is genuinely ambiguous. Build it there next.

C1_component_resolution_chain.does: object -> TADIR (package) -> TDEVC (component id) -> DF14L (application component)
C1_component_resolution_chain.why_it_matters: the strongest algorithm in the inventory because it is DETERMINISTIC: SAP states the answer instead of us pattern-matching a name. 1.61M objects resolvable.
C1_component_resolution_chain.failure_mode: a name-range chunk that returns exactly the cap truncates silently
C1_component_resolution_chain.improve: function modules resolve only via their function group; resolve them directly via TFDIR

C2_ascent_with_provenance_rung.does: climb from any object to the installation, ALWAYS recording which rung of the evidence ladder resolved it
C2_ascent_with_provenance_rung.why_it_matters: the rung IS the point — a curated assignment must never be presentable as an inference (CP-003). 92.2%.
C2_ascent_with_provenance_rung.failure_mode: measuring the percentage against the wrong denominator. s097: 182 synthesised concepts and 24 users counted as 'unresolved' when they can never carry a component.
C2_ascent_with_provenance_rung.improve: add recency — an object with no execution in the window is a different verdict from one with none at all

C3_static_edge_extraction.does: parse ABAP source for reads_tables / writes_tables / calls_fms and merge the edges into the graph
C3_static_edge_extraction.why_weak: only 98 of 1,212 objects carry code edges. Most of the graph is connected by crossings, not by parsed structure.
C3_static_edge_extraction.failure_mode: a WRONG edge is worse than a missing one — it sends someone to change the wrong thing. The parser is deliberately conservative: unambiguous SELECT/INSERT/CALL FUNCTION forms only, full-line comments stripped so a commented-out SELECT never becomes a dependency, dynamic forms skipped.
C3_static_edge_extraction.improve: the 134 code objects with NO source need ADT extraction — that is the real remaining gap
C3_static_edge_extraction.denominator_correction_s097: "98 of 1,212 objects have edges" measured the WRONG POPULATION — tables, GL accounts, variants and synthesised concepts cannot have code edges. Against CODE objects it was 86/245 (ABAP_REPORT 64%, ABAP_CLASS 78%). The remaining 159 split into a PARSER gap (25 with source on disk, closed in s097 — 8 yielded edges) and an EXTRACTION gap (134 with no source, needs ADT). Two different problems wearing one number. SECOND TIME this exact mistake appeared this session: the ascent had it too.
C3_static_edge_extraction.also_populated_by: the brain graph build, which produces the pre-existing edges

D1_D3_delta_strategies.does: PK-delta for master, value-compare for totals, high-water-mark for transactional
D1_D3_delta_strategies.why_it_matters: the intelligence is the ROUTING (table class -> strategy), not the strategies themselves
D1_D3_delta_strategies.failure_mode: the sync log records domain, table and strategy but NEVER the system — with one golden DB per system that ambiguity is now structural

D4_field_splitting.does: split a wide table read into column groups against the 512-byte line buffer, re-join locally
D4_field_splitting.failure_mode: a re-join on a non-unique key silently multiplies rows
D4_field_splitting.gated: GATED s097: the chunk PLAN and the positional MERGE were extracted to pure functions (plan_field_chunks, merge_chunks_by_position) and given 5 cases. The reading needs a connection; the plan does not, and the plan is where it can be wrong — a chunking that drops or reorders a field corrupts every row merged by position afterwards, and the corrupt rows look valid.

D5_bounded_probe_with_cap_reporting.does: read with an explicit cap and date filter; report a hit cap as '>=cap', NEVER as a count
D5_bounded_probe_with_cap_reporting.why_it_matters: the discipline IS the algorithm — a truncated read reported as a total is how a model starts lying
D5_bounded_probe_with_cap_reporting.failure_mode: the one it exists to prevent

E1_crossing.does: join profile x capability x claims x documents x companions through an explicit canonical key
E1_crossing.produces: system-level blind spots — modules the tenant runs that the model never examined
E1_crossing.failure_mode: comparing names raw instead of canonically. That defect appeared THREE times in one session.
E1_crossing.improve: the claim matcher still has a text fallback; report it as weak linkage rather than merging it with structured evidence

E2_coherence.does: compare what the macro asserts top-down against what the detail evidences bottom-up
E2_coherence.why_it_matters: the ONLY mechanism that detects the model drifting from the system it describes
E2_coherence.failure_mode: a defect in the checker reads as a defect in the model — which is what happened, and is why it must fail loudly

E3_trigger_evaluation.does: compare state against thresholds across accumulation / maturity / interpretation families; return what to re-run and why
E3_trigger_evaluation.failure_mode: thresholds chosen by judgement can be so loose nothing ever fires, which looks identical to a healthy model

E4_canonicalisation.does: resolve any spelling to a canonical key through a declared alias contract, in exactly one place
E4_canonicalisation.failure_mode: the defect it removes: reporting something MISSING that exists under an alias

F1_interface_boundary_analysis.does: enumerate the boundary (RFCDES / EDIDC / TBTCP / ICFSERVICE) and CORRELATE the configuration against observed traffic in the call stream. Configuration says what someone once set up; the call stream says what happens today; the GAP is the finding, in both directions.
F1_interface_boundary_analysis.why_it_matters: the boundary carries 1.33M executions and 37 documented flows, and the map is PROSE written by hand: it cannot detect a new destination appearing, cannot go stale visibly, and cannot be reproduced on a second installation (INSTANCE, not KIT)
F1_interface_boundary_analysis.improve: disambiguate the remaining truncated fragments by CALL SIGNATURE rather than by prefix: if a fragment calls the same function modules as exactly one full name, it is that name.
F1_interface_boundary_analysis.first_run: 238 destinations configured -> 10 LIVE, 228 DEAD (configured, zero traffic: maintenance and attack surface nobody uses), 249 UNDECLARED (traffic with no RFCDES entry). 9 IDoc message types / 19,400 documents. 5,822 active HTTP services. FULL scan, no sampling.
F1_interface_boundary_analysis.failure_mode: TRUNCATION: PARAMX is a FIXED-LENGTH field and SAP cuts the caller string when it does not fit — 'caller: host=HQ-SAP-P01_P01_00, dest=HQ-SAP-P01-1_P01_'. I had recorded this as 'the parse truncates names', which was WRONG ABOUT THE CAUSE: the regex extracts exactly what is stored, and no better pattern can recover a character the source never wrote. FIXED by reconciliation instead of parsing (caller_parse.py): a value that is a strict PREFIX of exactly one longer observed value is the same entity cut short. 81 repaired; 72 left AMBIGUOUS on purpose, because a fragment with two completions would be an invented fact. REMAINING: 'HQ-SAP-P0' carries 2.6M calls and is ambiguous — too many candidates share that prefix.

C1c_custom_fm_domain.does: custom Z/Y function module -> canonical domain, via the curated tfdir_custom.APP_DOMAIN overlay
C1c_custom_fm_domain.why_it_matters: custom FMs have no SAP component by definition, and they are precisely the objects the differentiation rests on. Y_BAPI_WBS_FINANCIAL_DATA_1 (974,868 calls) resolved to nothing until this rung existed — the single highest-volume business function module in the tenant was invisible to the model.
C1c_custom_fm_domain.failure_mode: the overlay is CURATED (3,073 FMs). An uncurated custom FM resolves to nothing and looks like a technical object.
C1c_custom_fm_domain.improve: derive the overlay from what each custom FM READS/WRITES rather than curating it by hand

F2_satellite_derivation.does: group boundary endpoints into SATELLITES by call signature, resolve what each calls, and bind it to the domains and flows it drives
F2_satellite_derivation.why_it_matters: each interface DEFINES a satellite; the satellite is the ORIGIN of the transaction; the origin is what associates it to a flow. In a system orchestrated 80% from outside, the satellite catalogue IS the process map at the boundary.
F2_satellite_derivation.first_run: 40 satellites from 7,783,106 calls; 12 GUID FLEETS RECOVERED. Independently rediscovered MuleSoft: a 21-endpoint fleet calling Y_BAPI_WBS_FINANCIAL_DATA_1 974,868 times -> PS -> PROJ2FUND, and a 17-endpoint fleet on Y_BAPI_YPS8 -> PS/PSM_FM -> B2C2A, P2P, POST2BUDGET, PROJ2FUND.
F2_satellite_derivation.failure_mode: endpoint names arrive TRUNCATED from SAP (PARAMX is fixed length), which split one satellite across several labels. FIXED in s097 via caller_parse: fleets recomposed from 17/21 endpoints to 7/6 once the truncated GUIDs merged with their full forms. What remains is the ambiguous tail — fragments with more than one possible completion are deliberately NOT merged, because a wrong merge invents a satellite.
F2_satellite_derivation.improve: fix the truncation, then merge fleets whose endpoint prefixes match | after A5 learned 17 rules the 19-endpoint fleet resolved from ? to FI (drives B2C2A, DISBURSE, O2C_BILLING) — evidence that re-running the cycle after a lower layer improves is not ceremony.

A7_concept_drift.does: monthly activity profile per domain as RATES PER DAY (executions, distinct objects, distinct users); a month is flagged when at least TWO signals depart from the trailing baseline by more than 50%. One signal moving is noise; two is a change of shape.
A7_concept_drift.why_it_matters: replaces the threshold heuristics in check_triggers with a question put to the log itself: did the process change, and when? A biennium organisation has an EXPECTED drift at the boundary; any other drift is the finding worth having.
A7_concept_drift.failure_mode: TWO defects found on its own first runs, both worth recording because both produce confident nonsense: (1) comparing monthly VOLUMES across unequal months produced 11 signals, almost all in the first FULL month — the window is 2026-02-21..2026-06-21, so February has 3 days and April 30. Fixed by normalising per day. (2) z-scores over a two-month baseline exploded to z=1016 because the standard deviation collapses. Fixed by using relative change, which is robust at n=2 and readable. An absurd number dressed as a statistic is worse than a plain one.
A7_concept_drift.current_reading: 3 signals, ALL in 2026-06, all 'distinct objects up', across UNRELATED domains (CTS_Transport, HCM, Basis_Security). Same month + same signal + unrelated domains is the signature of a CAPTURE CHANGE, not process drift. Recorded as a SUSPICION, not a finding.
A7_concept_drift.improve: needs about a year of history before a z-score is meaningful and before an expected biennium boundary can be told apart from an anomaly. It strengthens purely by the accumulator continuing to run — which is the argument for protecting A2. | PERFORMANCE: ~7 minutes per run because it scans all 15.6M audit rows with no index. It should aggregate per month INCREMENTALLY into a small table and read that. A slow algorithm gets skipped, and a skipped algorithm is documentation.

C4_object_role_derivation.does: derive what each object is FOR — posting engine, report, interface, worklist, master-data maintenance, checker, batch engine, technical — from signals we already hold: edges, execution channel, audience size, volume and text
C4_object_role_derivation.why_it_matters: the model could say where an object BELONGS and not what it DOES. 'PBC has 33 objects' is not knowledge; '2 posting engines, 14 reports, one operator on the worklist' is. A domain with readers and no writer is CONSUMED, not operated — and no list of names can say that.
C4_object_role_derivation.first_run: 178 objects: 55 REPORT, 46 POSTING_ENGINE, 27 MASTER_DATA_MAINTENANCE, 23 INTERFACE, 12 WORKLIST, 9 CHECKER, 4 TECHNICAL, 2 BATCH_ENGINE. INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATION of the operating model: PS, Travel, BusinessPartner, Procurement_P2P and Treasury_EBS all flagged DRIVEN FROM OUTSIDE — derived from object ROLES, not from the audit log's origin axis. Two independent methods agreeing is real validation.
C4_object_role_derivation.failure_mode: a role is a HYPOTHESIS. A report that writes a log table looks like a writer; a getter that posts looks like a reader. The confidence and the evidence are returned so a reader can disagree — a role asserted without its evidence would be worse than none.
C4_object_role_derivation.improve: feed it the flows: an object's role WITHIN a flow (approver, poster, reconciler) is sharper than its role in general

D6_aggregate_before_resolve.does: push the row reduction into SQL (GROUP BY), then resolve the expensive enrichment ONCE per distinct entity, and cache the aggregate against a watermark so a re-run with no new data costs nothing
D6_aggregate_before_resolve.why_it_matters: MEASURED 548x less Python work: 15,605,644 audit rows collapse to 33,607 (month,object) pairs over 26,131 distinct objects. 430s -> 187s cold -> 30s warm. And speed is not an optimisation here: a slow algorithm gets skipped, and a skipped algorithm is documentation — the model stops learning without anyone deciding it should. AND IT IS NOT ONLY SPEED: in interface_boundary the pattern made a full scan affordable, which removed a 400,000-row sample that had been producing WRONG verdicts — two destinations reported DEAD that are alive, and 209 undeclared callers hidden. A sample presented as a census is how a model lies quietly.
D6_aggregate_before_resolve.failure_mode: the aggregate must be keyed on a WATERMARK that actually moves. Cached against something static, it serves stale results forever and looks fast while being wrong.
D6_aggregate_before_resolve.constraint: the Golden DB is read-only by contract, so the cache lives OUTSIDE it. Adding an index would have been the other obvious fix and is not permitted.
D6_aggregate_before_resolve.improve: apply it to the other per-row enrichments: CDHDR (7.8M), cdhdr_history (12M), REGUH (3.7M), FMIOI (2.2M)
applied_to: process_mining/interface_boundary.py  removed a 400,000-row SAMPLE — and it CHANGED THE ANSWER
D6_aggregate_before_resolve.already_compliant: process_mining/rfc_process_classifier.py was ALREADY doing this before the pattern had a name: 'SELECT PARAM3, SLGUSER, COUNT(*) ... GROUP BY PARAM3, SLGUSER'. Naming a pattern sometimes just makes visible what a good instinct already did.
D6_aggregate_before_resolve.not_a_defect_today: CDHDR (7.8M), cdhdr_history (12M), REGUH (3.7M) and FMIOI (2.2M) were named as candidates in the ecosystem pattern. CHECKED: no current tool scans them row-by-row in Python. They are future risks to watch, not present defects — inventing work there would have been dishonest.
D6_aggregate_before_resolve.gated: GATED s097: the drift statistic was extracted from main() to departures_for() and BOTH of its real defects are now cases — constant per-day rate must produce NO signal (the volume-vs-rate defect, 11 false signals), and no magnitude may exceed 1000% (the z=1016 defect). Neither was caught by a check before, because inline code cannot be gated.

A8_change_to_executor_attribution.does: join a STATE-CHANGE stream to an EXECUTION stream on (user, day, hour) to derive WHAT WRITES a thing and through WHICH CHANNEL CHAIN. Scored by the phi coefficient over the slot contingency table, with an exclusivity constraint across classes. The channel is not a label but a CHAIN with evidence per link — DIALOG, RFC_INBOUND (naming the calling host/destination from PARAMX, which is the satellite), FILE (naming the paths), BATCH_JOB (naming the job that fires the program), PROGRAM — and every derived channel is cross-checked against the DECLARED taxonomy in integration_channels.json, kept in a separate field, with a verdict: CONFIRMED / UNCONFIRMED PROSE / UNDECLARED.
A8_change_to_executor_attribution.why_it_matters: It converts a change log into behaviour. The model could say a thing changed and who the user was; it could not say what did the writing — and for the largest object class in this tenant, 93% of the change documents carry NO transaction code, so the field that should answer is empty. This is the generic enrichment: any state-change log crossed with any execution log answers the same question. Which program sends this IDoc type. Which job produces this file. Which process touches this interface. It is not a PBC analysis that happened to work; it is the method.
A8_change_to_executor_attribution.first_run: 72 object classes, 3,280 programs, 2,493 hour-slots. Recovers known-correct writers as a control: RM_MEPO_GUI for EINKBELEG (purchase orders), RM_MEREQ_GUI for BANF (requisitions), the HR engine chain RHHCP_DC_EMPLOYEE / RHRFPM_ENGINE_PA30 for PBC and FMRESERV. SAPMSSY1 correctly demoted to AMBIGUOUS everywhere.
A8_change_to_executor_attribution.failure_mode: THREE SCORINGS WERE WRONG BEFORE ONE WAS RIGHT, and each failure is now a comment in the file. (1) RAW COINCIDENCE named a spool artifact as the writer of the largest class, because the RFC dispatcher runs constantly and coincides with everything. (2) LIFT fixed that and inverted the error: it rewards RARITY, so it ranked the real PBC engine below noise and filtered it out — HUNCALC0 runs on 91 of 108 days, so its base rate is 0.84 and its lift cannot exceed 1.19 however perfect the coincidence. An engine is not rare; running whenever the class changes is what makes it the engine. (3) Small denominators: a program that ran ONE day scored lift 27 on a single coincidence — the same defect as D6's z-score over a two-month baseline, in different clothes. The standing failure mode is that CO-OCCURRENCE IS NOT CAUSATION. Two programs in the same chain cannot be separated below the shared time granularity. Every row carries its evidence and a verdict so a human can disagree. FOURTH AND FIFTH FAILURES, both found on its own output: the channel was decided by whether a dispatcher reached the TOP of a ranking built to DEMOTE dispatchers — suppressing the signal and then looking for it where it had just been suppressed, so 71 of 72 classes came back as anything-but-interface. And the cross-check APPENDED the declared channel beside the derived ones, which silently promotes a sentence in a markdown table to the standing of a measurement and destroys the very comparison that makes either side worth having. Five wrong designs before one that holds.
A8_change_to_executor_attribution.improve: (a) the exclusivity constraint is a FLAG, not a solver — a real global assignment would sharpen every row at once; (b) join on the object key where the execution log carries one; (c) feed the named function modules straight into F1/F2 so a satellite inherits the tables it writes; (d) DBCON and WEBSERVICE are declared in the taxonomy but have no derivation yet — there is no DBCON table in the golden and ICF only says a service is active, not that it wrote.
A8_change_to_executor_attribution.gated: GATED s097: golden cases over phi() and the channel classifier, including the two scorings that were wrong — a daily dispatcher must score 0, and a program that covers nearly every change slot must NOT be filtered for being frequent.

A9_business_rules_from_source.does: extract the DECISIONS that live in code rather than in configuration — quasi-config literals, hard constants with their reasoning, intent comments, modification blocks with the transport that made them, which standard interfaces are overridden, and debug leftovers still in production
A9_business_rules_from_source.why_it_matters: a config-frontier analysis cannot see any of this, so a domain can look fully configured and still behave in a way nobody documented. The case that produced it: how far into the future a temporary position is financed is MV_EXTENSION_YEARS = 10 — a business decision as a constant, changed from 1 by a named transport, with the reasoning in a comment and an EXPIRY built into that reasoning. No table records it. It also recovered the BIENNIUM rule the capability model had recorded as unknown.
A9_business_rules_from_source.first_run: 25 production objects of package ZPBC: 3 quasi-config, 136 hard constants, 39 intent statements, 18 modification blocks with transports, 22 standard overrides, 120 leftovers
A9_business_rules_from_source.failure_mode: IT READS TEXT. A construct it does not recognise is simply not reported, so ABSENCE IN ITS OUTPUT IS NEVER EVIDENCE — which is the single most dangerous way to misuse it, because the output looks like an inventory. Every finding carries a line number so it can be confirmed against the source, and it must be, before anyone acts. It also cannot tell a live rule from dead code: `GET_SCENARIO` returning a constant and a commented-out branch look alike.
A9_business_rules_from_source.improve: (a) parse the branch conditions, not only the assignments — the vacancy rule was found by reading, not by the extractor; (b) diff the P01 corpus against the D01 corpus, so a rule that changed but never shipped is visible; (c) feed the modification transports into the transport intelligence, which already holds release dates
A9_business_rules_from_source.gated: GATED s097: golden cases over the modification-block parser and the quasi-config detector, including the exact D01K9B04Y9 block that started it

P1_profile_composition.does: compose the installation profile from 18 COMPONENTS, each bound to the algorithm that derives it, each carrying its own provenance — DERIVED, DECLARED or MISSING
P1_profile_composition.why_it_matters: the profile was HAND-MAINTAINED. profile_concept.json said so itself: 'who_updates: any session that measures something — EDIT unesco_system_profile.json'. A hand-edited profile cannot be reproduced on a second installation, cannot go stale visibly, and cannot say what it is missing. Composing it turns 'profile this system' from an exercise into a runnable list, and the DERIVED share is the honest portability number: 61% of the profile costs nothing on the next tenant, and the rest is named.
P1_profile_composition.first_run: 18 components — 11 DERIVED, 6 DECLARED, 1 MISSING. The MISSING one is security_posture: nothing in the repository derives it, which is the SAME gap the capability grid reports from the other side (E_AUTH empty in 16 of 21 domains). Two instruments agreeing that something is absent is worth more than a placeholder.
P1_profile_composition.failure_mode: IT COMPOSES, IT DOES NOT MEASURE. A component reads DERIVED because an artifact exists with content — not because that content is CURRENT or CORRECT. A stale artifact from six months ago composes exactly like a fresh one, so P1 must be read together with the cycle state and the drift signal, never alone. It also cannot tell a DECLARED value that is right from one that is wrong; it only says a human put it there.
P1_profile_composition.improve: (a) carry each artifact's mtime so a stale component is visible in P1 itself rather than only in the cycle state; (b) shrink the DECLARED set — every one converted to DERIVED is hand work removed from installation #2, and footprint and org_structure are the two closest, since probe_footprint.py already derives them and only the WRITE-BACK is manual; (c) build the security-posture derivation, the one genuine hole.
P1_profile_composition.gated: GATED s097: golden cases over the composition and the DERIVED/DECLARED split

A10_address_chain_reconstruction.operates_on: master data + fact tables + change logs
A10_address_chain_reconstruction.does: reconstruct the chain from funding source to piece of work in an installation where no foreign key carries it: infer the GRAMMAR of the identifiers, walk each declared HOP, and report per hop whether it resolves, through WHICH carrier, how much finer resolution survives, and whether any instrument can observe it changing
A10_address_chain_reconstruction.fires_on: check_triggers.py — the designed work carrier crossing zero, a NEW identifier grammar appearing, the fund or WBS master growing >=5%, or any chain object having no change-document coverage. Placed in run_analysis_cycle.py after extract_business_rules.py
A10_address_chain_reconstruction.why_it_matters: SUBSTITUTED is the verdict that pays for the algorithm: a link that works through a string convention or a custom table is invisible to anyone reading the data model, so it is never migrated, never documented, and never load-tested — and it is load-bearing
A10_address_chain_reconstruction.failure_mode: scoring a carrier against a population it was never meant to serve, which reads as a broken chain and is a mis-stated denominator; and a discovered change-document class claiming a table on a shared prefix. Both were real defects in the first run, fixed with breakdown-by-grammar and one-to-one assignment
A10_address_chain_reconstruction.improve: derive the hops from the golden's own key structure instead of declaring them, so a new installation gets a first pass with no spec at all

A11_shared_algorithm_memory.does: hold what each algorithm LEARNED about the substrate — which log is a filtered subset, which connection drops, which declared column is blank in every row — so the next algorithm starts from it instead of rediscovering it or, worse, drawing a conclusion from an instrument it did not know was partial
A11_shared_algorithm_memory.fires_on: continuously — every algorithm calls recall() before choosing its instruments and remember() after establishing a fact. It is not scheduled; it is a dependency
A11_shared_algorithm_memory.why_it_matters: algorithms.json records what each algorithm IS. This records what each one LEARNED. Only the second one compounds — without it every algorithm pays the same discovery cost forever
A11_shared_algorithm_memory.the_rule: a memory carries subject, fact, who learned it, the evidence, and what OTHER algorithms should do differently. A memory with no implication is a note, and notes are not machine-actionable
A11_shared_algorithm_memory.failure_mode: a stale memory is worse than none — the substrate changes. Re-learning the same subject by the same algorithm SUPERSEDES rather than duplicates
A11_shared_algorithm_memory.improve: expire a memory whose evidence is older than the window the claim depends on

A12_set_hierarchy_traversal.does: walk a SAP set hierarchy to every leaf, then answer the three questions that decide whether a roll-up is safe: which master values roll up NOWHERE, which repeat INSIDE one tree, and which appear across SEVERAL root trees. Only then report what each level consumes
A12_set_hierarchy_traversal.fires_on: after any SETS extraction, and whenever an organisational roll-up is to be reported
A12_set_hierarchy_traversal.why_it_matters: nothing in the fact tables references a hierarchy — the roll-up exists only in configuration, so 'what does this sector spend' has no mechanical answer until the sets are traversed. And the answer is unusable until the orphans are counted
A12_set_hierarchy_traversal.failure_mode: three real ones, all found in the first run. Defining a root as 'appears as a parent' drops FLAT sets and reports their whole master as 100% orphaned. Counting every repeated membership as double-counting turns biennium VERSIONING into a fake defect. And identifying a set class by matching leaf values invites numeric collision — class 0303 matched the fund-centre master at 79.3% and is a cost-centre hierarchy
A12_set_hierarchy_traversal.improve: resolve non-numeric leaf RANGES against the master instead of marking them unenumerable

A13_custom_field_harvest.operates_on: source code crossed with the golden
A13_custom_field_harvest.does: harvest every customer-namespace field this installation added to the standard model, attribute it to its table where the code says so, record HOW it is used, and pair that with whether anything is IN it
A13_custom_field_harvest.fires_on: before designing anything that needs a new field, and after any extraction that adds a standard table — the population half of the answer moves with the golden
A13_custom_field_harvest.why_it_matters: an EMPTY custom field is an extension point that already exists in the dictionary, already survived every upgrade, and is already in the tables a future design would write to. Not knowing them means rebuilding what is there or colliding with it
A13_custom_field_harvest.the_state_that_is_not_empty: FIELD_NOT_EXTRACTED and TABLE_NOT_EXTRACTED mean UNMEASURED. Reporting them as empty is a confident wrong answer, so they are a distinct state carrying the list of tables to re-pull
A13_custom_field_harvest.failure_mode: the first version matched only TABLE-FIELD and missed every field used in a WHERE clause without a prefix. ZZFIX_RATE, which gates the entire budget-rate mechanism, was absent from the first run — that absence is now the algorithm's self-test
A13_custom_field_harvest.improve: read DD03L from the system for the authoritative list rather than inferring existence from usage

A14_budget_rate_impact.operates_on: FM actuals crossed with FI and the rate tables
A14_budget_rate_impact.does: compute the budget-rate impact the way the organisation defines it — FM at the fixed rate minus the same base at the standard rate — by replicating the four baselines GET_BR_IMPACT selects between, and reporting per route rather than as one number
A14_budget_rate_impact.fires_on: whenever the budget-rate impact is asked for, and after any extraction that adds FI or rate data
A14_budget_rate_impact.why_it_matters: the organisation already computes this in YFM_FI_COMPARE_INCLUDING_BR. Reconstructing the definition from outside when one exists is how two correct calculations disagree — so this mirrors their code
the_four_routes: WRTTP 51 + RMBE + BTART 0200 -> EKBE goods receipt, negated
KURSF when set — not the path in practice; the comparison is on AMOUNTS
otherwise rate type M at the posting date — the UN operational rate
A14_budget_rate_impact.failure_mode: three real ones, all found by running it. Quoting an impact from ONE route: route 1 has most LINES, route 4 most MONEY on the actuals side, and route 2 lives in a DIFFERENT TABLE — the commitments — so searching the actuals returns 'no population' and it is false. Comparing a per-LINE amount against a per-ITEM baseline: EKBE is per purchase-order item and several lines share one, which inflated the standard side by 35%. And treating a NEGATIVE rate in TCURR as a multiplier: it is an indirect quotation and means divide.
A14_budget_rate_impact.improve: implement route 2 against EKBE; the current perimeter has no population for it

A15_subject_graph.does: relate the pieces of a subject as a graph of typed edges, where every node points at where its content lives and the graph carries only the RELATION and the evidence for it
A15_subject_graph.fires_on: after a subject has been learned in fragments across a session, and whenever a new conclusion lands that should relate to the others
A15_subject_graph.why_it_matters: each fragment landed correctly in its own store; what did not exist was the RELATION. A conclusion with no edges is prose with a JSON wrapper — the edges are what let 'what does the availability check depend on' be answered mechanically instead of re-derived
gates: every node's content_in must RESOLVE to a real file or record
an ORPHAN node (no edge) is reported — it means the relation is missing
a DANGLING edge is reported — it names a node that does not exist
A15_subject_graph.failure_mode: the resolver split the reference on '.' and truncated every real filename at its extension, reporting two working references as broken. A gate with false positives is worse than no gate
A15_subject_graph.improve: generalise beyond one subject — take the subject name and its stores as arguments

A16_payroll_end_to_end.operates_on: the payroll engine — configuration that reads like data
A16_payroll_end_to_end.does: discover payroll end to end in six parts: the ENGINE (schemas), the LOGIC (rules), the OUTPUT (wage types, grouped by stem), the GATES (features), the MASTER DATA including whether it is maintained by hand or fed, and the POSTING path with the enhancements sitting on it
A16_payroll_end_to_end.fires_on: whenever staff cost, a payroll calculation or an HR-to-FI posting question arises — and once per installation as part of the profile
A16_payroll_end_to_end.the_premise_it_is_built_on: PAYROLL LOGIC IS NAMED AFTER WHAT IT PRODUCES. Searching the schemas and 166,453 rule lines for the budget rate returned one false positive; grouping wage types by stem found it immediately — 72 'Constant Dollar' members under stem 9. So the discovery runs from the OUTPUT backwards as well as from the driver forwards
A16_payroll_end_to_end.why_it_matters: payroll is neither ABAP nor data, so a code search does not reach it and a table search does not recognise it. It computes the largest spend category in most public-sector installations and was a black box here
the_two_questions_that_are_not_an_invent: is this master data maintained BY HAND or FED? — a change document with a transaction code was made by a person in a screen; a BLANK transaction code is the signature of a BAPI, an interface or a batch, and the ratio is the answer
who enhanced the POSTING path? — a posting program is the seam between payroll and accounting, and the custom enhancements there are the shortest description of what an installation actually changed
A16_payroll_end_to_end.failure_mode: reporting an inventory and calling it a process. Listing schemas is easy; the flow through them, and the manual-versus-fed split on master data, are what make it usable
A16_payroll_end_to_end.improve: follow the schema flow from the driver through COPY and PIT steps to build the actual execution order, and cross the posting runs against FI document headers

A17_change_governance.operates_on: the change log crossed with the execution log and the transport record
A17_change_governance.does: detect three governance conditions: a CHANNEL DIFFERENCE where an object is reached by a route its other maintainers do not use, CONFIGURATION changed in production that has never travelled by transport, and a transport channel carrying DATA rather than development
A17_change_governance.fires_on: per close, and whenever a governance or segregation question arises
A17_change_governance.the_premise_that_makes_it_portable: THE POPULATION OF MAINTAINERS DEFINES THE NORM. No policy document is needed and none is asked for — whatever route most people use for an object is the expected route. That is what lets the same detector run on any installation
A17_change_governance.every_finding_carries_its_counter_explan: a channel difference is a SIGNAL, not a verdict. Number ranges are not transported by SAP design; a new implementation is naturally driven from the editor before its transaction is rolled out; role generation legitimately carries its generated tables

two_kinds_of_channel_finding.SOLE_USER_OF_A_GENERIC_ROUTE: one person reaches the object through the editor while the others use a transaction
two_kinds_of_channel_finding.GENERIC_ROUTE_IS_THE_NORM: the MODAL route for the object IS the editor — the stronger finding, and the one the first version missed because it only looked for outliers

A17_change_governance.failure_mode: two, both found by running it. Listing business DOCUMENTS as 'never transported' — true and useless, since transactional data does not travel; fixed by splitting configuration from documents on volume and maintainer count. And missing the case where the generic route is the modal one, which is worse than an outlier, not better
A17_change_governance.improve: resolve the program behind a generic route from the execution log automatically

_portfolio._reading: Twelve algorithms have no market equivalent — that is the defensible surface. Eight are adopted standards, correctly, because reinventing DFG discovery would be vanity. The single MISSING one covers the integration boundary, and the single FRAGILE one is the log accumulator, which is simultaneously the most valuable algorithm here and the least protected.
_portfolio._s098: A10 and A11 added. A10 answers 'which funding source paid for which work' where no key says so; A11 is the memory that lets every algorithm inherit what the others learned.

_priorities.1: A2 — protect the log accumulator. FRAGILE, unversioned, and the only algorithm whose value is destroyed by delay.
_priorities.2: golden cases for the unguarded algorithms — 20 of 22 can regress silently today.
_priorities.3: B4 — normative models for the public-sector flows; authored, not yet implemented.
_priorities._note: F1 was priority 1 and is now built. The mechanism (improve_algorithms.py) re-ranks these from measured signals rather than from memory.

_doctrine_how_to_build_better_algorithms._why_here: the reasoning that produces the next algorithm must live with the algorithms, not in a conversation
_doctrine_how_to_build_better_algorithms.premise: Algorithms are not one asset among others — they are the ONLY asset that survives the client. Data ages from the moment it is extracted. Findings age: '80.6% external' is true for Feb-Jun 2026. Tools are bindings — p2p_conformance.py is one algorithm tied to one flow, one schema, one tenant. The ALGORITHM is what travels to installation #2.
_doctrine_how_to_build_better_algorithms.move_1_change_the_substrate_not_the_algo: OCEL 2.0 instead of a flat log: the SAME discovery algorithms, radically better fidelity on convergent processes. Public-sector finance is convergent constantly — one budget, many commitments, many actuals. A flat log forces an artificial case ID and distorts exactly what we need to see. Cheapest and highest-leverage of the three.
_doctrine_how_to_build_better_algorithms.move_2_add_the_axis_the_market_lacks: A3 is this move already: process mining assigns activities but does not systematically resolve WHO CALLED. In a system orchestrated 80% from outside, the caller IS the process. Adding a dimension to a proven algorithm is cheaper and more defensible than inventing one.
_doctrine_how_to_build_better_algorithms.move_3_author_the_normative_content: We do not compete by building a better conformance checker — the market has one and reinventing it is vanity. We compete by being the only ones who know what 'correct' means for budget→commitment→actual. The ALGORITHM is theirs; the public-sector NORMATIVE CONTENT is ours. That is where the moat is.
_doctrine_how_to_build_better_algorithms.move_4_declare_the_failure_mode: Every algorithm states how it LIES, not only what it does. The market ships algorithms as black boxes. In a domain where being confidently wrong is expensive, publishing the failure mode is itself a differentiator — and it is the only thing that makes an algorithm reviewable.

_new_asset_classes_s097._note: ranked by value. Classes 1-3 now exist; class 4 is a declared slot.

1_normative_models.why: B4 conformance is the heart of the product and is worthless without something to measure against. One normative model existed before this (P2P 3-way match); the four public-sector flows had none.

2_event_log_definitions.why: the table→event mapping (case_id, activity, timestamp, resource) per flow is reusable across clients and is invisible today

3_failure_modes.status: CREATED as a field on every algorithm; queryable view pending
3_failure_modes.why: 'in how many known ways can this model lie?' is the question an auditor asks and no vendor answers

4_benchmarks.status: SLOT — cannot be filled before client #2
4_benchmarks.why: 'in a UN agency, staff cost is X% of budget'. The slot must exist NOW: without it the second client gets analysed as if it were the first and the comparison is lost.

_nesting._insight: USER, s097: algorithms are NESTED. You start from the standard, then the logs, then discover interfaces and correlate — and each interface or connection DEFINES A SATELLITE, which gives you the ORIGIN of the transaction, which is what associates it to a flow and a domain.
_nesting._why_it_was_wrong_before: the catalogue was a FLAT LIST organised by operand. But an algorithm's output is another's input: this is a directed graph. Treating it as a list is why F1 (boundary) and A3 (origin axis) ran INDEPENDENTLY — F1 enumerated destinations, A3 parsed raw host strings — and a fleet of 174 middleware endpoints collapsed into one label because A3 had no satellite catalogue, only strings.

L0_INVARIANT.note: the ground truth every other answer is anchored to. Improving it lifts everything above.

L0b_CUSTOM_OVERLAY.note: custom Z/Y function modules have NO SAP component by definition — their function group lives in a customer package DF14L cannot resolve. They need their own rung, and they are exactly the objects the product thesis rests on because no commercial tool can label them either.

L1_OBSERVATION.note: what runs, when, by whom — classification anchored on the standard

depends_on: L0/L0b (to resolve what each satellite calls)
L3_ORIGIN.note: a satellite is an ENTITY, not a caller string: identity, channel, volume, direction, the domains it touches

L4_FLOW.note: process mining runs per FLOW, never per module

L5_CONFORMANCE.note: worthless without the normative model — which is why that asset class exists

_consequences.1: an algorithm CANNOT be better than its dependencies. A3's origin resolution is capped by F1's quality — today F1 truncates destination names, so A3 inherits that error.
_consequences.2: improving a LOW layer lifts everything above it. The L0 fix (DF14L instead of regex) took the frontier from 40% to 7.7% without touching any algorithm above it.
_consequences.3: the improvement mechanism must weight by DEPTH, not only by state. improve_algorithms.py does not yet — that is a declared gap.

_nesting.A8_change_to_executor_attribution: L2 — consumes the accumulated logs (A1/A2) and feeds F1/F2: attribution names the channel, and an INTERFACE channel names the functions that define a satellite

_improvement_axes._note: improve_algorithms.py ranks by HEALTH — unguarded, stale, fragile. That is maintenance. These four axes rank by DISTANCE TO THE GOAL, which is a product that instantiates on another organisation and explores its domains autonomously.
_improvement_axes.1_from_classification_to_investigation: our algorithms answer 'what is this?' but none generates its own next question. mine_domain.py exists and is barely used; the registry is still hand-curated (128 objects vs 286 auto-resolved). A5 is the only algorithm that learns.
_improvement_axes.2_from_observation_to_modelling_a_flow: we can see execution; we cannot yet build an event log for a flow nobody hand-configured. To model B2C2A we would write it by hand — that does not scale to 8 flows x N clients. The event-log DEFINITIONS must become an asset.
_improvement_axes.3_from_n1_to_generalisable: EVERY algorithm is validated on ONE tenant. 43 golden cases, all UNESCO facts. COMPONENT_TO_DOMAIN is a hand-written map reflecting UNESCO's module set. MEASURED: only 22.7% of resolved executions are tenant-invariant; 2,617,419 rest on 334 hand-curated entries.
_improvement_axes.4_from_confident_to_calibrated: DONE s097 — resolve_domain() now returns (domain, confidence, rung, evidence, tenant_invariant). Before this, an answer SAP asserts and an answer we curated were indistinguishable to every consumer. An algorithm that cannot say HOW it knows cannot be triaged, audited, or ported — and cannot be improved deliberately, because you cannot tell a lucky answer from a sound one.
_improvement_axes._the_measure: brain_v2/methods/measure_portability.py — the low-confidence answers ARE the map of what breaks next.
